sample_unit: patient cases (head and neck cancer notes from MIMIC-IV-Note)

links.outcome: Expert-rated hallucination audit and reasoning scores, guideline-informed retrieval pipeline versus vanilla LLM
links.effect: Hallucination Audit rose from 3.90±1.32 to 4.74±0.76; Overall Reasoning rose from 3.40±0.90 to 4.00±0.73 (p<0.001). Effect is confounded with structured prompts and self-refinement.
links.quote: Domain scores increased for Clinical Knowledge Application (2.87±1.20 to 3.70±1.03), Contextual Understanding (3.48±0.95 to 3.98±0.95), Hallucination Audit (3.90±1.32 to 4.74±0.76), Reasoning Transparency (3.45±1.02 to 3.86±0.87), and Chain-of-Thought Quality (3.32±1.04 to 3.69±1.00), all p≤0.001.

unlisted_practices: structured prompting with specialty-specific reasoning pipelines

screen.reason: Evaluates whether adding guideline-informed retrieval and self-refinement scaffolding to an LLM improves clinical reasoning, transparency, and hallucination reduction on real EHR cases judged by clinicians.
